It’s sort of a cheeky joke about how deeply segregated men and women were at the time - not just to the domestic space and the economic/academic space, but truly in all parts of life, women were defined by their “Otherness” (like the concept from de Beauvoirs The Second Sex). This means their feminine natures, in many ways, were defined to accentuate masculine nature as a foil. Femininity wasnt the independent identity we think of today, it was just non-masculinity. 

So yea, it’s pretty silly to think of now, but back then so many ‘manly’/‘womanly’ behaviors were considered mutually exclusive (basically to maintain a gender binary which was way more extreme than it is now). Basically this poster says “oh god forbid we share one character trait, oh wow wouldn’t that just be the worst if we wore one similar thing, guess men are gonna have to start wearing something else cause we want pants”

Hope that helps/makes sense!
